security_problem: A valid tools/call can reach the downstream stdio or remote transport even when its final allow event was never durably appended to the hash-linked JSONL audit ledger: Logger.Log swallows write/short-write errors and advances chain state before the write is known to have succeeded, and all three terminal allow branches forward unconditionally after best-effort logging. Additionally, chain state was recovered from a separate pre-open path read while appends go through a different fd, so a rotated/rebound configured audit path can either carry a stale recovered chain onto a fresh inode or authorize a commit written through a stale fd whose inode no longer matches the configured path. Round 5 adds four further fail-closed gaps: (1) a same-inode hard-link or symlink rebind can authorize a commit with zero parent-directory durability, so a power loss can leave the path bound to an un-fsynced directory entry; (2) an ordinary Log continues appending after the logger has been poisoned by any write/validation/sync failure, extending an incomplete JSON record or forking the chain with the unchanged predecessor/index; (3) a constructor sync failure pathname-unlinks the configured path, which can delete an atomically installed replacement owned by another writer; and (4) every constructor open follows a pre-existing symlink, so a malicious link at the configured audit path makes the logger open and append to an unrelated regular victim file. Round 6: validateDurableBindingLocked uses os.Stat, which follows symlinks, so a rotator can move the opened ledger to another directory on the same filesystem, replace the configured path with a symlink to that moved inode, pass os.SameFile, and receive fsync only for the directory containing the symlink; the target directory entry can be lost after power failure, leaving a dangling configured path even though the allow was relayed.
required_behavior: For every valid tools/call C, downstream_transport_received(C) implies a full, hash-linked EventToolAllowed record for C completed on the configured regular O_SYNC JSONL ledger before the downstream write began. Logger.CommitAuthorization accepts only terminal allow events, requires a regular durable sink, performs a full-write check, poisons the logger on write/short-write failure, and advances hash-chain state only after success. NewLogger recovers or initializes the hash chain from the exact O_SYNC append fd: a fresh exclusive-create always starts at genesis; an existing inode is recovered through the fd that will receive appends; every authorization commit validates live fd regularity and that the configured path itself is a non-symlink regular directory entry referencing the constructor-bound inode (no-follow Lstat) immediately before and immediately after its write, failing closed (ErrAuditSinkChanged/ErrNonDurableSink) on any rotation, rename, unlink, replacement, observed symlink including a same-inode symlink, or non-regular rebinding, poisoning the logger, and leaving in-memory chain state unchanged. Every accepted constructor binding (fresh create or existing inode) is accepted only after its containing parent directory has been fsynced, and both pre-write and post-write binding validations also fsync the parent directory, so a same-inode hard-link rebind may be accepted only through that directory-durability boundary; any observed symlink, including one resolving to the opened inode, returns ErrAuditSinkChanged, poisons the logger, leaves chain state unchanged, and prevents relay; any parent-directory sync failure in a constructor or commit validation poisons the logger and leaves chain state unchanged. Ordinary Log returns ErrAuditSinkUnhealthy immediately after any poison source and never writes again. A constructor sync failure never pathname-unlinks anything: the inode/path is left as found and a later successful constructor revalidates and resyncs an existing binding. Every constructor open uses kernel no-follow semantics so a pre-existing symlink sink is rejected at construction and its target is never modified. Approved, explicit, and default/fallback allow branches commit before returning "forward"; any commit failure produces a generic client deny and zero stdio/remote relay. Metrics and session taints mutate only after commit success. Omitted/invalid AuditLogPath fails closed.
failure_behavior: Fail closed: sink failure, short write, closed logger, non-durable sink, poisoned logger, or a rotated/rebound configured audit path (missing, renamed, unlinked, replaced, atomic-renamed-over, any observed symlink including a same-inode symlink, or non-regular) denies the valid tools/call with no relay on either transport, no allow/approved metric, no session taint, and no in-memory chain advance. A same-inode hard-link rebind that cannot be made durable through parent-directory fsync, any observed commit-time symlink at the configured path including one resolving to the opened inode, a pre-existing symlink at the configured audit path (rejected at construction, target bytes unchanged), an ordinary Log attempted after any poison, and a constructor sync failure that would have pathname-removed a potentially foreign replacement also fail closed.
